toolDetails.name: get_skill_execution_updates
toolDetails.description:
STREAMING RENDER LOOP. This tool returns a slice of a live output stream.
Everything in `items[]` is finished, user-facing text that CLAIRE already
produced. Render it to the user BEFORE calling this tool again.

DO NOT accumulate items across polls and write one summary at the end.
That is the primary failure mode for this tool. The user is waiting on
each slice; a correct final answer delivered all at once is still wrong.

## Loop

Call this after invoking a skill with `deferred: true` that returned
`status: "IN_PROGRESS"`.

  1. Render every item in `items[]` per the contract below.
  2. Wait `pagination.poll_interval_ms` (default 1000).
  3. Call again with `pagination.cursor` passed back verbatim;
     keep `message_id` and `conversation_id` unchanged.
  4. Stop when `status` is terminal (SUCCESS | PARTIAL_SUCCESS | FAILED)
     AND `pagination.has_more` is false.

First call: `message_id` and `conversation_id` come from `context` in the
initial response; `cursor` is "0". An empty `items[]` is normal — poll again.
`render_note` is present only when there is output to emit.
Do not call other tools between polls unless the user asks something new.

## Rendering contract (mandatory)

Render in arrival order. Never summarize, paraphrase, translate, reorder,
omit, restructure, rename, or truncate a frame.

  REASONING_TRACE    Verbatim, prefixed "CLAIRE reasoning:"
  EXECUTION_INSIGHT  Verbatim, prefixed "Step:"
  TOKEN              Buffer `payload.content` between the enclosing
                     STREAM_STATUS STARTED and COMPLETED; emit the
                     concatenated text as one block on COMPLETED.
                     Never emit individual fragments. A run may span
                     polls — keep the buffer across calls.
  STREAM_STATUS      Not rendered; drives the TOKEN flush.
  HUMAN_PROBE        Verbatim. Stop polling and wait for the user's reply.
  PLAN               Plan text verbatim, then list `suggestedPrompts`.
  ARTIFACT           Render ea

The stakeholder must belong to the specified role. To filter the results of a name match, specify stakeholder_email. When you identify a role by its name, the role must apply to the type of the asset. If you provide both an identity and a name, the tool uses the identity. Names are case sensitive. servers.name: CDGC Data Quality Score
servers.description: Retrieves data-quality scores for governed catalog assets in Cloud Data Governance and Catalog (CDGC).

toolDetails.name: get_asset_score
toolDetails.description:
Returns the persisted DQ score for one governed CDGC asset via id + scheme (internal/external).

If you only have a name: resolve it to an id via the CDGC Metadata Search MCP (either scheme) first. Report by core.name and core.externalId, never the UUID.

Classify from systemAttributes.core.classType OR the most-specific systemAttributes.type - one or the other, not both.

If the type is not one of the 15 supported: Data Element, Technical Dataset, Business DataSet, Business Term, Metric, System, SubDomain, Domain, Policy, Process, Rule Template, Legal Entity, Geography, Business Area, Project - reply 'not supported for DQ scoring' and stop.

If it is a Rule Occurrence (RuleInstance/RO): no dataQuality. Score = selfAttributes com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.value, banded by Target/Threshold; totalCount = rows, exception = failed rows. RuleType and dimension are NOT returned - infer from core.name, else 'unknown'. Report score (2 dp), total/failed rows, dimension, refresh date.

Else (supported non-RO type): dataQuality has one entry per dimension - core.score (0-100), core.scoreTrend, ruleCount, ScoreAggregationBuckets (counts per band Good/Acceptable/Not Acceptable). Freshness = latest core.modifiedOn; not real-time, updates only after CDGC's next aggregation run. Default: report only the overall score (2 dp, mean of per-dimension core.score) plus freshness, one line. Mean is the only derived value; per-dimension scores are read as stored, never recomputed. Offer the per-dimension breakdown (score, band, ruleCount, trend), render only when asked.

Descendants: a core.DataElement or core.DataSet (Technical Dataset/Table) lists its ROs (classType=RuleInstance); other parents don't.

Edge case: wrong/missing scheme or unknown id returns {} at HTTP 200 - not-found, not an error.

toolDetails.name: run_published_taskflow
toolDetails.description:
⚠️ DEPRECATED — Replaced by run_taskflow_with_guid, which runs a published Taskflow by asset GUID. Use `run_taskflow_with_guid` instead. Runs a published taskflow, identified by its Run API name, and returns the new execution's run identifier. The request body carries the taskflow's input fields, which vary per taskflow.

Note: The run identifier is returned in the capitalized RunId field inside RunTaskFlowResponse. Downstream taskflow tools such as get_taskflow_status, resume_taskflow_fault_retry, resume_taskflow_fault_skip, and terminate_taskflow_runs expect the same value in the lowercase runId or runid field. Callers must map RunId to runid when chaining a run into a status, resume, or terminate call.

toolDetails.name: run_published_taskflow_with_paramset
toolDetails.description: Starts a published taskflow under a named parameter set and returns its RunId. This tool does not accept taskflow input fields; the run uses the values from the parameter set and the taskflow defaults.

toolDetails.name: run_replication_task
toolDetails.description: Runs a data replication task identified by its task ID, task name, or federated task ID that includes the folder path.

toolDetails.name: run_synchronization_task
toolDetails.description: Runs a data synchronization task that keeps a source and target in sync, identified by its task ID, task name, or federated task ID.

toolDetails.name: run_taskflow_with_guid
toolDetails.description: Starts a run of a taskflow identified by its asset GUID (the design-time asset id, not the published Run API name). The call is asynchronous: it only confirms the run was submitted and does not return a run identifier, and an unknown GUID can still return a successful response. Use search_completed_jobs, list_running_jobs, or get_taskflow_status afterwards to locate the run and follow its progress. This endpoint cannot pass input fields to the taskflow.

toolDetails.name: search_completed_jobs
toolDetails.description:
Returns completed Data Integration jobs with run execution details, completion state, source and target row counts, error messages, and transformation statistics.

The response is a tree that starts at the connection root and expands every ancestor down to the requested path: find the container whose xpath equals the path you sent. Its containers are the sub-folders (names end with '/'; each xpath is already in the correct form to pass back as path to drill down) and its records are the files (bare names). A sub-folder shown inside a response is not expanded: its containers and records are always empty, which does not mean the folder is empty. To see what a sub-folder holds, call browse_objects again with that sub-folder's xpath as path, and never report a sub-folder as empty without browsing it. For Amazon S3, to describe or preview a listed file N, use objectName = that container's xpath minus its trailing '/' + '//' + N (at the bucket root: bucket + '/' + N). No pagination — very large folders return every entry in one response. toolDetails.name: create_connection
toolDetails.description: Create a connection in your organization. The body is a single flat 'connection' object, NOT the get_connector_schema tree. To build a correct body: (1) list_connector_types to identify the connector and pass its 'name' as 'type'; (2) get_connector_schema to learn which attributes apply, which are mandatory/secret, their options, and — for value-dependent attributes — which subgroup branch to send; (3) list_connection_runtime_environments for a valid top-level 'runtimeEnvironmentId'; (4) for toolkit/CCI connectors, resolve_dynamic_attributes fills option-driven values. Placement: standard/well-known attributes (username, password, host, port, database, schema, codepage, authenticationType, and similar) go TOP-LEVEL; only connector-specific attributes with no first-class field go inside connParams, keyed by attribute 'name'. Putting a standard attribute in connParams makes the server ignore it. The most reliable approach is to mirror an existing connection of the same 'type' from list_connections/get_connection_by_name. Never send agentGroupId/orgId/agentId (server-derived). Validate with test_connection before creating.

toolDetails.name: delete_connection

toolDetails.name: get_connector_schema

Call this after list_connector_types and before create_connection/update_connection to learn exactly which connector-specific attributes (connParams) a connector requires and what shape their values must take. Attributes tagged 'dynamicAttribute' have option lists that must be fetched at runtime via resolve_dynamic_attributes.

toolDetails.name: get_object_metadata

Sends objectName as a query parameter so multi-segment names with raw forward-slashes (including object-store `//`-encoded nested keys) are supported. Optional query flags: isFileList=true asks the connector to enumerate a directory-of-files object; engineType routes the metadata call to a specific runtime engine. For structured formats (Avro, Parquet, JSON, XML) use get_object_metadata_with_dataformat; for delimited flat files (CSV / tab-separated) use get_object_metadata_with_flatfile_attrs. APP_13400 is CDI's generic metadata-failure code, so act on its description text: 'invalid path element' means correct the path once; 'Insufficient privileges' or 'SQL access control error' means the connection cannot read that object, so report it to the user; an unreachable channel service or Secure Agent, a JDBC communication error, or 'error [null]' means the connection itself is broken, so run test_connection_by_id and report its result; 'entry [...] already exists' naming an object you did not ask for means an argument was sent blank or a path was mis-encoded, so resend it with every argument non-blank and each path or objectName encoded as its parameter description says. Do not keep retrying the same call with other path spellings.

Use for structured formats (Avro, Parquet, JSON, XML) registered under a CCM formatId. Sends objectName as a query parameter so multi-segment names with raw forward-slashes are supported. Optional query flags: isFileList=true asks the connector to enumerate a directory-of-files object; engineType routes the metadata call to a specific runtime engine. Use get_object_metadata_with_flatfile_attrs for delimited flat files (CSV / tab-separated), and plain get_object_metadata when no overlay is needed. APP_13400 is CDI's generic metadata-failure code, so act on its description text: 'invalid path element' means correct the path once; 'Insufficient privileges' or 'SQL access control error' means the connection cannot read that object, so report it to the user; an unreachable channel service or Secure Agent, a JDBC communication error, or 'error [null]' means the connection itself is broken, so run test_connection_by_id and report its result; 'entry [...] already exists' naming an object you did not ask for means an argument was sent blank or a path was mis-encoded, so resend it with every argument non-blank and each path or objectName encoded as its parameter description says. Do not keep retrying the same call with other path spellings.

toolDetails.name: resolve_dynamic_attributes
toolDetails.description: Resolve the live option list for a toolkit/CCI connector's dynamic attributes (attributes tagged 'dynamicAttribute' in get_connector_schema). Applies only to toolkit-based connectors and requires a runtime environment with an active Secure Agent, because the options are fetched from the connector running on that agent. Returns a flat list of attributes with their currently valid options.

toolDetails.name: test_connection
toolDetails.description: Test connectivity for a connection payload without persisting it. Supply the same flat 'connection' body you would pass to create_connection (a top-level 'name', 'type', 'runtimeEnvironmentId', the standard attributes top-level, and connector-specific attributes in connParams). Use this to validate attribute placement and credentials before creating or updating: a structured error such as 'Enter a valid user name' or 'The password is empty' means a required attribute was omitted or misplaced into connParams instead of top-level. Secrets must be real plaintext values for the test (a masked '********' fails). Live connectivity runs through the connection's runtime environment, so a resolvable runtime environment with an active agent is required.

toolDetails.name: test_connection_by_id
toolDetails.description: Test connectivity of an EXISTING, already-saved connection by its id. Unlike test_connection, this sends no body: the server loads the persisted connection (its stored, already-encrypted secrets and attributes) and runs a live connectivity check through its runtime environment. Use this to re-verify a connection you created or fetched (for example after create_connection, or a connection returned by get_connection / list_connections) without re-supplying any attributes or connParams. A resolvable runtime environment with an active Secure Agent is required; a failed check returns an error body with a code and description.

toolDetails.name: update_connection
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Update an existing connection in your organization. Send the full connection body as a single flat 'connection' object, NOT the get_connector_schema tree. Start from the current connection (get_connection) and mirror its top-level-vs-connParams placement. Standard/well-known attributes (username, password, host, port, database, schema, codepage, authenticationType, and similar) stay TOP-LEVEL; only connector-specific attributes with no first-class field go inside connParams, keyed by attribute 'name' — a standard attribute placed in connParams is ignored. Use get_connector_schema to learn which attributes/branch apply and which are mandatory/secret, list_connection_runtime_environments for a valid top-level 'runtimeEnvironmentId', and (toolkit/CCI) resolve_dynamic_attributes for option-driven values. Leave a secret unchanged by sending back the masked value '********' exactly; send a new value to change it. Never send agentGroupId/orgId/agentId (server-derived). Validate with test_connection before updating.

toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Starts an import job in the target environment, applying conflict resolution policies and optionally reusing target objects as dependencies. Returns an import job ID.

toolDetails.name: search_assets
toolDetails.description: Searches the catalog using a FIQL query to locate projects, folders, or assets. Returns FRS IDs and paths for export or import.

servers.name: IPU Management
servers.description: Enables AI agents to export IPU usage data grouped by organization, project, asset, or job in IDMC, and to track corresponding export jobs.

toolDetails.name: get_metering_export_job_status
toolDetails.description: Checks the status of an export job for IPU usage data by job ID. Reports progress each time, and reports job details when the job is complete.

toolDetails.name: request_asset_metering_export
toolDetails.description: Starts an asynchronous job to export IPU usage data grouped by asset and optionally filtered by meter ID, for a date range up to 30 days. Returns a tracking job ID.

toolDetails.name: request_job_metering_export
toolDetails.description: Starts an asynchronous job to export IPU usage data grouped by job and optionally filtered by meter ID, for a date range up to 180 days. Returns a tracking job ID.

toolDetails.name: request_metering_summary_export
toolDetails.description: Starts an asynchronous job to export IPU usage data grouped by organization for a date range up to 180 days. Returns a tracking job ID.

toolDetails.name: request_project_metering_export
toolDetails.description: Starts an asynchronous job to export IPU usage data grouped by project path within each organization for a date range up to 30 days. Returns a tracking job ID.

servers.name: User Management
servers.description: Enables AI agents to automate IDMC user onboarding, role provisioning, and offboarding to accelerate user access, eliminate manual IT overhead, and enforce least privilege security policies.

toolDetails.name: add_groups_to_user
toolDetails.description: Assigns one or more user groups to a user account in an IDMC organization, granting the group-level permissions defined for those groups.

toolDetails.name: add_roles_to_user
toolDetails.description: Assigns one or more roles to a user account in an IDMC organization, granting additional asset privileges.

toolDetails.name: create_user
toolDetails.description: Creates a user account in an IDMC organization and assigns roles or user groups. Requires at least one role or group assignment and automatically sends an activation email when you omit the password.

toolDetails.name: delete_user
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Permanently deletes a user account from an IDMC organization using the user ID. This tool is destructive and irreversible. Always ask for user confirmation before calling this tool.

toolDetails.name: get_role_details
toolDetails.description: Retrieves details for roles in an IDMC organization, with options to filter by role ID or role name and expand associated privileges.

toolDetails.name: get_user_details
toolDetails.description: Retrieves user account details for users in an IDMC organization, with options to filter by user ID or user name.

toolDetails.name: get_user_group_details
toolDetails.description: Retrieves details for user groups in an IDMC organization, with options to filter by user group ID or user group name. Each group record includes its assigned roles and member users.

toolDetails.name: remove_groups_from_user
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Removes one or more user groups from a user account in an IDMC organization, revoking the associated group-level permissions. This tool is destructive. Always ask for user confirmation before calling this tool.

toolDetails.name: remove_roles_from_user
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Removes one or more roles from a user account in an IDMC organization, revoking the associated privileges. This tool is destructive. Always ask for user confirmation before calling this tool.

servers.name: Audit Management
servers.description: The Audit Management server lets AI agents browse IDMC audit and security logs.

toolDetails.name: search_audit_log
toolDetails.description:
Browses the audit log. Each entry captures the acting user, the object affected, and timestamps in both Eastern (ET) and UTC time. The category parameter classifies the audited object domain. The event parameter classifies the action performed.
Do not include parameters to view the most recent 200 entries. Include batchId and batchSize parameters to page through results, where batchId 0 is the most recent batch. For example, batchSize 25 with batchId 1 returns entries 26-50.

toolDetails.name: search_security_log
toolDetails.description:
Browses security log entries. The following are security log entries:
- Login and logout actions
- Multi-factor authentication (MFA) enable, disable, and verification events
- Password resets
- Creation, update, and deletion of users, user groups, and roles
Do not include parameters to view security log entries from the previous 24 hours with a maximum of 200 entries.
You can include an RSQL-style q filter that joins any of the following conditions with ';' (AND):
- entryTime. A UTC range spanning at most 14 days.
- actionCategory
- actor
- objectName
Any q field other than entryTime requires an entryTime range.
Use skip and limit parameters to page through larger result sets. The default skip is 0. The default limit is 200. The limit range is between 100 to 1000.
The search_security_log tool has read-only access to logs. This tool never creates, modifies, or revokes users, roles, or access.

servers.name: Address Verification
servers.description: Provides real-time data quality assurance by validating and standardizing using the Cloud Address Verification service.

toolDetails.name: verify_address
toolDetails.description: Provides real-time data quality assurance by validating and standardizing using the Cloud Address Verification service.

servers.name: CAI Administration
servers.description: Manages Application Integration process schedules, URN mappings, and tenant email settings through the CAI cai-administration APIs.

toolDetails.name: create_schedule
toolDetails.description: Creates a new process schedule in the caller's organization, to run an IPD or BPEL service on a recurring interval or a one-time trigger.

toolDetails.name: delete_schedule
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes one or more process schedules from the caller's organization, identified by scheduleId.

toolDetails.name: delete_urn
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes one or more URN mappings from the caller's organization, identified by URN name. If the user has not given the tenant id, resolve it with the resolve_tenant_id_from_jwt skill (the org_id claim of the OAuth access token) instead of asking.

toolDetails.name: duplicate_schedule
toolDetails.description: Creates a copy of one or more existing schedules, identified by scheduleId, each with a new scheduleId.

toolDetails.name: edit_schedule
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Updates an existing process schedule in the caller's organization, identified by scheduleId.

toolDetails.name: get_email_config
toolDetails.description: Retrieves the caller's tenant email (SMTP notification) settings. This is an org-level setting: if any process faults, a mail is sent to this address. Password fields are masked in the response.

toolDetails.name: get_schedules_by_id
toolDetails.description: Retrieves one or more process schedules from the caller's organization by scheduleId.

toolDetails.name: get_urn_definitions
toolDetails.description: Retrieves the URN mappings defined for the caller's organization, resolving logical URNs used inside processes to concrete URLs. If the user has not given the tenant id, resolve it with the resolve_tenant_id_from_jwt skill (the org_id claim of the OAuth access token) instead of asking.

toolDetails.name: list_schedules
toolDetails.description: Lists process schedules belonging to the caller's organization. If the user has not given the tenant id, resolve it with the resolve_tenant_id_from_jwt skill (the org_id claim of the OAuth access token) instead of asking.

toolDetails.name: reload_schedules
toolDetails.description: Reloads the schedule engine's in-memory cache for the caller's organization, picking up out-of-band changes. Requires a JSON body, even an empty object.

toolDetails.name: run_schedule
toolDetails.description: Triggers one or more schedules to run immediately, identified by scheduleId, outside their normal recurrence.

toolDetails.name: set_schedule_state
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Enables or disables one or more schedules, identified by scheduleId. A disabled schedule remains defined but stops firing.

toolDetails.name: update_email_config
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Updates the caller's tenant email (SMTP notification) settings, replacing the current configuration. This is an org-level setting: if any process faults, a mail is sent to this address.

toolDetails.name: upsert_urn
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Adds new URN mappings or updates existing ones for the caller's organization. If the user has not given the tenant id, resolve it with the resolve_tenant_id_from_jwt skill (the org_id claim of the OAuth access token) instead of asking.

servers.name: CAI Asset Management
servers.description: Lists, publishes, unpublishes, and updates Application Integration processes and connections, searches the catalog, and audits deployments in the organization.

toolDetails.name: deployment_audit
toolDetails.description: Returns a one-shot snapshot of deployment activity in the caller's organization, each collection trimmed to its most useful fields plus its total row count. Read-only. Returns: processes (id, name, activeVersion, hasCurrentPlan) with processTotal; services (id, name, binding, processName) with serviceTotal; deployment log entries (id, name, date, deployerId, contributionId, errorCount, warningCount) with logTotal. Who deployed: deployerId on each log entry is the user who ran that deployment, and the log entry name is the deployed file, for example Process2.bpr. Processes and services do not carry a deployer, so to find who deployed a process, match the log entry by name or contributionId, or call search_contributions with deployerId. Not included: process group, plan counts, retention settings, service policies, and the log text; use the underlying search tools for those. Optional input tenantContextId scopes all three searches to that organization/tenant (omit it to scope to the caller's own tenant). Optional input maxReturn caps how many rows each of the three collections returns (omit it to use the server's own default page size). Each of the three searches is fixed to the first page only (listStart 0); this tool returns only that first page per collection — if the organization has more rows than fit on one page, use the underlying search_deployed_processes / search_deployed_services / search_deployment_logs tools directly to paginate through the rest.

toolDetails.name: get_asset_job
toolDetails.description: Retrieves the overall state and progress counts of a publish or unpublish job; poll after publish_assets or unpublish_assets until jobState is SUCCESS or ERROR. Returns only aggregated counts; use get_asset_job_status for per-asset results.

toolDetails.name: get_asset_job_status
toolDetails.description: Retrieves the per-asset status of a publish or unpublish job; poll until jobState is SUCCESS or ERROR, then report each item's outcome.

toolDetails.name: get_asset_path
toolDetails.description: Returns the asset path of an Application Integration asset (process, app connection, process object and so on) given its GUID. You must use this tool to obtain the asset path and must never guess or hand-write it: the path depends on the Project and Folder the asset currently sits in, which only this lookup reveals. Get the GUID first from list_assets or list_assets_in_location (the GUID field), then call this tool with it. The result contains assetPath in the form Explore/{Project}/{Folder}/{name}.{TYPE}.xml (the Folder segment is left out for an asset that sits directly in a Project), plus the asset name, type, Project and Folder. Pass assetPath as-is to publish_assets or unpublish_assets, which identify assets by asset path. The name is the asset's display name, which is also the DisplayName in list_assets (not its Name). Read-only with no side effects. If the GUID does not match any asset the call fails with a not-found error (code FRS_070); in that case re-read the GUID from list_assets instead of retrying with a guess.

toolDetails.name: get_trace_level_info
toolDetails.description: Retrieves trace and logging level information for a specific deployed process version, identified by its owning tenant, process namespace, and process name. If the user has not given the tenant id, resolve it with the resolve_tenant_id_from_jwt skill (the org_id claim of the OAuth access token) instead of asking.

toolDetails.name: list_assets
toolDetails.description: Lists Application Integration assets in the organization. Each asset returns: Guid (id), Display name (name), API Name (the APIName entry of customAttributes.stringAttrs, a list of name/value pairs), Project/Folder (parentInfo: Space, Project, optional Folder, each with parentName and parentType) and Publication status (the publicationStatus entry of customAttributes.stringAttrs: published or unpublished; absent for non-process assets). Narrow the list with one $filter condition on name or documentType (see $filter). Page with $top and $skip. Run a process by its API Name, not its display name: two assets can share a display name but never an API Name.

toolDetails.name: list_assets_in_location
toolDetails.description: Lists the assets (processes, app connections, process objects) in a Project, or in a Folder of a Project, so you can see what exists at a location before acting on it. Give the Project name in project, plus the Folder name in folder for assets inside a Folder; omit folder for assets directly in the Project (assets in its Folders are not included). Names are case-sensitive. Results are paged: limit defaults to 50 and offset to 0, and the result carries totalCount and hasMore, so keep requesting with offset increased by limit until hasMore is false. Each asset is returned with name, type, GUID and assetPath, in the form Explore/{Project}/{Folder}/{name}.{TYPE}.xml (no Folder segment for Project-level assets). Use the assetPath with publish_assets or unpublish_assets, or the GUID with update_assets. To search by name across the whole organization, use list_assets. If the Project or Folder does not exist, the result has an error message and the names that are available instead of assets; an existing location with no assets returns an empty assets list.

toolDetails.name: publish_assets
toolDetails.description: Starts a bulk publish job for asset paths taken from get_asset_path; then poll get_asset_job_status with the returned id until the job is final.

toolDetails.name: search_catalog
toolDetails.description: Searches design-time catalog resources (deployed configuration and data files such as app-config and cached entity lists) in the caller's organization. Set maxReturn and listStart to page; without them every match is returned, which can be large with includePublic. totalRowCount is an estimate here (completeRowCount is false). If the user has not given the tenant id, resolve it with the resolve_tenant_id_from_jwt skill (the org_id claim of the OAuth access token) instead of asking.

toolDetails.name: search_contributions
toolDetails.description: Searches deployed contributions (deployed BPR packages) in the caller's organization, optionally filtered by URI, version, deployer, process group, or deployment date range. If the user has not given the tenant id, resolve it with the resolve_tenant_id_from_jwt skill (the org_id claim of the OAuth access token) instead of asking.

toolDetails.name: search_deployed_processes
toolDetails.description: Searches deployed processes (deployment plans) in the caller's organization, optionally filtered by name or process group. Returns totalRowCount, so an empty result with a total of 0 means nothing matched. If the user has not given the tenant id, resolve it with the resolve_tenant_id_from_jwt skill (the org_id claim of the OAuth access token) instead of asking.

toolDetails.name: search_deployed_services
toolDetails.description: Searches deployed service definitions (partner link bindings exposed by deployed processes) in the caller's organization. If the user has not given the tenant id, resolve it with the resolve_tenant_id_from_jwt skill (the org_id claim of the OAuth access token) instead of asking.

toolDetails.name: search_deployment_logs
toolDetails.description: Searches deployment log entries for contributions in the caller's organization, optionally filtered by contribution, file name, log severity (errors or warnings), or date range. Entries do not include the log text; read a single entry by id for that. If the user has not given the tenant id, resolve it with the resolve_tenant_id_from_jwt skill (the org_id claim of the OAuth access token) instead of asking.

toolDetails.name: search_indexed_properties
toolDetails.description: Searches indexed properties (queryable fields exposed by deployment plans for correlation and reporting) in the caller's organization. Takes no paging parameters and returns every match without a total count. If the user has not given the tenant id, resolve it with the resolve_tenant_id_from_jwt skill (the org_id claim of the OAuth access token) instead of asking.

toolDetails.name: unpublish_assets
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Starts a bulk unpublish job for asset paths taken from get_asset_path; then poll get_asset_job_status with the returned id until the job is final.

toolDetails.name: update_assets
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Updates settings on processes or app connections identified by GUID. Set assetType and fill the matching collection (processes or connections). Keys are exact and case-sensitive; unknown keys are silently ignored, so confirm the change took effect. A multi-valued key replaces the whole list; omitted keys are left unchanged. If any asset fails, the call returns HTTP 500 with status FAILED. Description, connection name and connector type cannot be changed.

servers.name: CAI Connection Management
servers.description: Lists listener-based event connections and starts or stops their event-source routes in Application Integration through the CAI event-connection APIs.

toolDetails.name: list_event_connections
toolDetails.description: Lists listener-based event connections (event sources) in the caller's organization. Each result is a connection (connectionName) with its event routes in connectionDetails; each route carries eventRoute (the value to pass to start_event_connection and stop_event_connection), eventRouteType (protocol), eventRouteStatus, eventsConsumed, and last modified details. Covers cloud-hosted and Secure Agent-hosted connections. There is no server-side status filter, so read eventRouteStatus from the results. Without maxReturn only the first 10 entries are returned, so set maxReturn to 9999 to get everything in one call. Paging is applied by the backend to route rows before they are grouped, so listStart is not a clean connection offset: a connection can appear again on the next page, and a page can be empty even when more routes exist. If you do page, deduplicate routes by eventRoute and do not use a short page as proof that you reached the end. The reliable way to narrow a large result is the connectionName and eventRouteType filters.

toolDetails.name: start_event_connection
toolDetails.description: Starts an event source in a listener-based connection so it begins receiving events and triggering its process. Works for both Secure-Agent-hosted connections (pass agentName) and cloud CamelOnCloud/EIP-hosted connections (omit agentName; the call is proxied to the EIP service, which must be enabled and cluster-healthy). Use the exact eventRoute value returned by list_event_connections.

toolDetails.name: stop_event_connection
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Stops a running event source in a listener-based connection so it stops receiving events. Works for both Secure-Agent-hosted connections (pass agentName) and cloud CamelOnCloud/EIP-hosted connections (omit agentName; the call is proxied to the EIP service). Use the exact eventRoute value returned by list_event_connections.

servers.name: CAI Job Management
servers.description: Monitors, controls, and troubleshoots running Application Integration process instances — status, logs, faults, and lifecycle actions — through the CAI process APIs.

toolDetails.name: complete_process
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Force-completes a process instance immediately, without executing its remaining activities. This cannot be undone and skips the remaining work, so confirm with the user first.

toolDetails.name: count_process_log_events
toolDetails.description: Returns the number of process log events matching the given filters, without returning the events themselves. Returns a bare plain-text integer, not a JSON object.

toolDetails.name: count_processes
toolDetails.description: Returns the number of process instances (runs, not definitions) that match all of the filters given, without returning the instances. Every filter is optional and filters combine with AND; with none, it counts every instance. Returns a bare plain-text integer, not a JSON object. How to pass filters: processName is a whole-name match ignoring case (use * for a wildcard); processState is one upper-case state; times are ISO-8601 UTC timestamps such as 2026-11-03T15:51:54Z, with createdFrom/createdTo bounding when instances started and completedFrom/completedTo bounding when they finished. Example, runs of Process2-1 in the last 24 hours: processName=Process2-1 and createdFrom=<current UTC time minus 24 hours>. Example, failed runs today: processState=FAULTED and createdOn=<today's date>.

toolDetails.name: delete_process
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes a single completed, faulted, or terminated process instance and its stored runtime data. Irreversible.

toolDetails.name: delete_processes_by_filter
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes every process instance matching a search filter (name, group, or state). Irreversible; an empty filter deletes all instances, so always supply a scoping field.

toolDetails.name: delete_processes_by_ids
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes multiple process instances in one call, given an explicit list of process ids. Irreversible.

toolDetails.name: get_anonymous_process_openapi_spec
toolDetails.description: Returns the OpenAPI 3.0 specification of a published CAI process that is exposed anonymously, describing the request body it accepts and the response it returns. Call this before run_anonymous_process to learn what input to pass as payload. Fails with 403 if the process requires sign-in; use get_process_openapi_spec for that. To find the process name, use list_assets on the cai_asset_management server and read the API name field. search_deployed_processes also lists deployed names, but in a namespace-qualified form that you must strip.

toolDetails.name: get_deployment_plan
toolDetails.description: Retrieves the compiled deployment plan of a deployed process definition, which is the version servicing new and running instances. The response is the compiled BPEL source, not plan metadata; use search_deployed_processes for deployment metadata.

toolDetails.name: get_process_attachment
toolDetails.description: Retrieves a binary or document attachment produced or consumed by the process instance during execution, as a downloadable file rather than a JSON envelope.

toolDetails.name: get_process_coordinator
toolDetails.description: Retrieves BPEL coordination details for a process instance acting as a coordinator, including the participant instances it coordinates. Empty for non-coordinating instances.

toolDetails.name: get_process_detail
toolDetails.description: Retrieves full detail for a single process instance: state, state reason, name, namespace, timing, and the fuller record beyond list_processes summary fields.

toolDetails.name: get_process_full_log
toolDetails.description: Retrieves the full, verbose execution log for a process instance as a downloadable log file. Try get_process_log first for a summary.

toolDetails.name: get_process_log
toolDetails.description: Retrieves the condensed execution log for a single process instance as a single log string, rather than structured per-event entries.

toolDetails.name: get_process_openapi_spec
toolDetails.description: Returns the OpenAPI 3.0 specification of a published CAI process that requires sign-in, describing the request body it accepts and the response it returns. Call this before run_process to learn what input to pass as payload. Fails with 403 if the process is anonymous or you have no access to it; use get_anonymous_process_openapi_spec for an anonymous process. To find the process name, use list_assets on the cai_asset_management server and read the API name field. search_deployed_processes also lists deployed names, but in a namespace-qualified form that you must strip.

toolDetails.name: get_process_participant
toolDetails.description: Retrieves BPEL coordination details for a process instance acting as a participant, including the coordinator it reports to. Empty for non-coordinated instances.

toolDetails.name: get_process_state
toolDetails.description: Retrieves the current lifecycle state of a process instance, e.g. RUNNING, SUSPENDED, FAULTED, or COMPLETED, with its state reason.

toolDetails.name: list_alarms
toolDetails.description: Lists the alarm (deadline/timer) queue: process instances waiting on a scheduled deadline, filterable by process or deadline window.

toolDetails.name: list_message_receivers
toolDetails.description: Lists the message receiver queue: instances waiting to receive a correlated message on a partner link, filterable by process or operation.

toolDetails.name: list_process_log_events
toolDetails.description: Searches individual process log events, filtered by process, severity, or date range, to find specific errors without pulling a whole log.

toolDetails.name: list_processes
toolDetails.description: Lists process instances (individual runs, not process definitions) in the caller's organization that match all of the filters given. Filters combine with AND. How to pass filters: processName is a whole-name match ignoring case (use * for a wildcard); processState is one upper-case state; times are ISO-8601 UTC timestamps such as 2026-11-03T15:51:54Z, with createdFrom/createdTo bounding when instances started and completedFrom/completedTo bounding when they finished. Use it to find a process instance id, or to see exactly which runs a count_processes call counted (pass the same filters). Results are paged: maxReturn defaults to 20, and listStart is the zero-based offset of the first result.

toolDetails.name: resume_process
toolDetails.description: Resumes a previously suspended process instance, letting it continue from where it was paused. To recover a faulted instance, use retry_process, resume_process_with_fault_retry, or resume_process_with_fault_skip.

toolDetails.name: resume_process_with_fault_retry
toolDetails.description: Resumes a faulted process instance by retrying the faulted activity with the input it originally received. This resumes the instance, which is a lifecycle change; retry_process retries the activity without changing the lifecycle state.

toolDetails.name: resume_process_with_fault_skip
toolDetails.description: Resumes a faulted process instance by skipping the faulted activity and continuing with the next activity. The work of the skipped activity is not performed.

toolDetails.name: retry_process
toolDetails.description: Resolves the currently faulted activity of a process instance by retrying it, without changing its lifecycle state. To resume the instance as well, use resume_process_with_fault_retry.

toolDetails.name: run_anonymous_process
toolDetails.description: Starts a new run of a published CAI process that is exposed anonymously, so no sign-in is needed to call it. Pass the process input in payload, shaped like the request schema from get_anonymous_process_openapi_spec; omit payload for a process that takes no input. Fails with 403 if the process requires sign-in; use run_process for that. To find the process name, use list_assets on the cai_asset_management server and read the API name field. search_deployed_processes also lists deployed names, but in a namespace-qualified form that you must strip. Each call starts a new instance and is not idempotent. The reply is the process's own output and carries no process id.

toolDetails.name: run_process
toolDetails.description: Starts a new run of a published CAI process that requires sign-in, by calling its endpoint as the current user. Pass the process input in payload, shaped like the request schema from get_process_openapi_spec; omit payload for a process that takes no input. Fails with 403 if the process is anonymous or you have no access to it; use run_anonymous_process for an anonymous process. Each call starts a new instance and is not idempotent. To find the process name, use list_assets on the cai_asset_management server and read the API name field. search_deployed_processes also lists deployed names, but in a namespace-qualified form that you must strip. The reply is the process's own output and carries no process id.

toolDetails.name: step_process_activity
toolDetails.description: Executes the activity at a given BPEL location in a debug-suspended process instance to step it forward. Requires location; omitting it silently does nothing.

toolDetails.name: suspend_process
toolDetails.description: Pauses a running process instance, halting all further activity execution until it is resumed with resume_process. To end an instance permanently, use terminate_process.

toolDetails.name: terminate_process
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Cancels a single running or suspended process instance immediately. Irreversible; the instance cannot be resumed afterward.

toolDetails.name: terminate_processes
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Cancels multiple process instances in one call, given an explicit list of process ids. Irreversible.

servers.name: Catalog Asset History
servers.description: The Catalog Asset History server lets you investigate how enterprise data assets change over time in Data Governance and Catalog. Use it to see who changed an asset, what they changed, and when, including attribute edits, relationship updates, certification decisions, and stakeholder assignments.

toolDetails.name: get_asset_history
toolDetails.description:
Retrieves the change history, or audit trail, for a catalog asset, showing who changed what and when, with before and after values.

Call get_asset_details first to obtain the asset identity.

Use offset to page through older events.

Returns change events, each with a timestamp, eventId, action, eventType, and the resolved createdBy and modifiedBy users. Asset and relationship events also include a changes array of per-attribute edits. In each change, "from" is the prior value and "to" is the new value, and operation is CREATE, OVERWRITE, or DELETE. On the wire, omits "from" for a new attribute and omits "to" for a removed attribute. The side that is present indicates the direction of the change.

The mode field indicates how the change was captured: REALTIME means a live, interactive change. BATCH means a bulk or batch ingestion job.

For certification events, certification.certificationValue is true when the asset is certified and false when it is decertified.

The __restricted field is true when the entire asset is hidden by access control. In this case, the event is returned as a stub that contains only the identity and classType. The __restrictedAttributes field lists specific attributes that are hidden by policy on an otherwise visible asset.

servers.description: Lists, inspects, runs, exports, and deletes data profiles on catalogued data sets in Cloud Data Governance and Catalog (CDGC).

servers.name: Data Access Management
servers.description: Manages data access control, filtering, and de-identification policies within Informatica's Cloud Data Governance and Catalog (CDGC).

toolDetails.name: create_business_term
toolDetails.description: Creates a business term (core.classType=BusinessTerm) used as glossary context in data access policy conditions.

toolDetails.name: create_data_access_control
toolDetails.description: Creates a data access control policy that grants read, write, or delete access to specific tables or views in the target source system through pushdown enforcement.

toolDetails.name: create_data_deidentification
toolDetails.description: Creates a data de-identification policy that applies data protections to fields or cells, ordered by an existing precedence tier.

toolDetails.name: create_data_filter
toolDetails.description: Creates a data filter policy that denies access to rows matching a rule condition, enforced in-place or through pushdown to the source system.

toolDetails.name: create_data_protection
toolDetails.description: Creates a data protection, a reusable set of data de-identification techniques such as tokenization, hashing, or redaction, applied to specific data types.

toolDetails.name: create_precedence_tier
toolDetails.description: Creates a precedence tier that ranks how data de-identification policies are evaluated, ordered from the lowest rank to the highest.

toolDetails.name: create_usage_type
toolDetails.description: Creates a usage type (usage context), such as 'Data-Access-Management' or 'Reporting and Analytics', referenced by policy conditions. Belongs to the Data Marketplace service, not the Data Access Management policy API.

toolDetails.name: delete_data_access_control
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes a data access control policy by its internal ID. Grant revocation on the source system after deletion is not documented. Verify on the source system that grants were revoked.

toolDetails.name: delete_data_deidentification
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes a data de-identification policy by its internal ID.

toolDetails.name: delete_data_filter
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes a data filter policy by its internal ID.

toolDetails.name: delete_data_protection
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes a data protection by its internal ID. Deletion of a referenced protection is not guarded against. Before you delete a data protection, check for references from data de-identification policies to prevent creating orphaned data protections.

toolDetails.name: delete_precedence_tier
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes a precedence tier by its internal ID. Deletion of a tier that is still referenced is not guarded against. To prevent creating orphaned policies, check for references from data de-identification policies before you delete a precedence tier.

toolDetails.name: get_data_access_control
toolDetails.description: Retrieves a single data access control policy by its internal ID.

toolDetails.name: get_data_deidentification
toolDetails.description: Retrieves a single data de-identification policy by its internal ID, including its precedence tier and per-field protections.

toolDetails.name: get_data_filter
toolDetails.description: Retrieves a single data filter policy by its internal ID.

toolDetails.name: get_data_protection
toolDetails.description: Retrieves a single data protection by its internal ID, including its configured data de-identification techniques.

toolDetails.name: get_precedence_tier
toolDetails.description: Retrieves a single precedence tier by its internal ID, returning either the published or draft copy.

toolDetails.name: list_data_access_controls
toolDetails.description: Lists published data access control policies for lookups.

toolDetails.name: list_data_classifications
toolDetails.description: Lists the data element classes such as SSN or email, in the catalog so you can use their IDs in data filter and data access control policy conditions. Only classifications already assigned to technical assets by a catalog scan can be referenced by policies. Pass a name or keyword in knowledgeQuery, or '*' to list all. Page with from and size.

toolDetails.name: list_data_deidentifications
toolDetails.description: Lists published data de-identification policies for lookups.

toolDetails.name: list_data_filters
toolDetails.description: Lists published data filter policies for lookups.

toolDetails.name: list_data_protections
toolDetails.description: Lists published data protections for lookups when building data de-identification policies.

toolDetails.name: list_precedence_tiers
toolDetails.description: Lists published precedence tiers with their IDs, names, and ranks for lookups and reference maps.

toolDetails.name: list_usage_types
toolDetails.description: Lists usage types by ID and name, for resolving the usage types referenced in policy condition constants before building data filter policies or data de-identification policies.

toolDetails.name: list_user_groups
toolDetails.description: Lists IDMC user groups so you can use a group ID in a data access control rule condition (context::principal.groups). Filter by group name or ID with `q`, and page with limit and skip. Specify a group that exists in the organization or the policy is rejected.

toolDetails.name: publish_data_access_asset
toolDetails.description: Submits a draft data access asset for workflow review and activation. Data access assets are precedence tiers, data protections, data filter policies, data de-identification policies, or data access control policies.

toolDetails.name: search_policy_reference_assets
toolDetails.description: Searches the catalog for business terms or data element classes to resolve a name to its internal ID for use in policy conditions and field locator queries. Scope the search with filterSpec (core.classType=BusinessTerm for terms, core.classType=core.DataElementClassification for classes). Data element classes must already be assigned to technical assets through catalog scans before policies can reference them.

toolDetails.name: update_data_access_control
toolDetails.description: Partially updates a data access control policy, for example its description. Editing a published policy creates an inactive draft until re-published with publish_data_access_asset.

toolDetails.name: update_data_deidentification
toolDetails.description: Partially updates a data de-identification policy, for example its description or precedence tier. Editing a published policy creates an inactive draft until re-published with publish_data_access_asset.

toolDetails.name: update_data_filter
toolDetails.description: Partially updates a data filter policy, for example its description or rules. Editing a published policy creates an inactive draft until re-published with publish_data_access_asset.

toolDetails.name: update_data_protection
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Replaces a data protection's full definition. This resource supports PUT only. Send the complete object, including any unchanged fields to prevent losing changes.

toolDetails.name: update_precedence_tier
toolDetails.description: Partially updates a precedence tier, for example its description or rank. Editing a published tier creates an inactive draft until re-published with publish_data_access_asset.

servers.name: Data Exploration Skill
servers.description: Single-tool MCP exposing the CLAIRE dataSkill — query raw dataset content such as rows, columns, values, and quality metrics.

servers.name: Data Integration Job Management
servers.description: Orchestrate, monitor, and manage the lifecycle of Data Integration tasks and taskflows, with live run status and an operator toolkit delivered as MCP resources.

servers.name: Data Marketplace Config
servers.description: Configures and maintains Cloud Data Marketplace (CDMP) artifacts, including categories, data collections, and delivery targets.

servers.name: Data Marketplace Order Management
servers.description: The Data Marketplace Order Management server lets AI agents manage the Data Marketplace order workflow.

toolDetails.name: approve_order
toolDetails.description: Approves a pending order so that it can proceed to fulfillment. Optionally records a comment explaining the approval.

toolDetails.name: cancel_order
toolDetails.description: Cancels an order, preventing it from proceeding further in the fulfillment process. Optionally records a comment explaining the cancellation.

toolDetails.name: create_order
toolDetails.description: Creates an order requesting access to a data collection in Data Marketplace. The order captures the target data collection, usage context, requested delivery target, business justification, cost center, and any custom attributes. You can only create orders for yourself.

toolDetails.name: delete_order
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes an order that was placed accidentally or is no longer needed. To delete a fulfilled order, first delete its associated consumer access.

toolDetails.name: fulfill_order
toolDetails.description: Marks an approved order as fulfilled. When the data is ready for delivery, the stakeholder delivers the data to the requester through the chosen delivery target. A stakeholder invokes this action.

toolDetails.name: get_order
toolDetails.description: Retrieves the details of a single order using its system-generated unique identifier. By default, the server returns basic order information. Use the attributes query parameter to expand the response with additional detail groups. Use any of the following groups: `customAttributes`, `dataCollection`, `stakeholdership`, `systemAttributes`, `terms`, `usageContext`. Use `all` for every group.

toolDetails.name: list_orders
toolDetails.description: Retrieves a paginated list of orders from Data Marketplace. Expand results with additional attribute groups, paged using offset and limit, and sorted by an available field.

toolDetails.name: reject_order
toolDetails.description: Rejects a pending order, indicating that it will not be fulfilled. Optionally records a comment explaining the rejection.

servers.name: Data Profiling Skill
servers.description: Single-tool MCP exposing the CLAIRE data_profiling skill — profiles a dataset to reveal structure, column statistics, patterns, and value distributions.

servers.description: Single-tool MCP exposing the CLAIRE data_quality_analysis skill — analyzes DQ rule execution results and scorecard metrics.

servers.name: Data Quality Rule Recommendation Skill
servers.description: Single-tool MCP exposing the CLAIRE data_quality_rule_recommendation skill — recommends and applies existing DQ rules to a data asset.

servers.name: Data Quality Scores
servers.description: Imports and retrieves data quality scores for rule occurrences using Cloud Data Governance and Catalog (CDGC).

servers.name: DI Resource Job Management
servers.description: Runs, stops, and recovers every Data Integration job type through tools, and exposes MCP resources for live job status (running jobs, per-run status for every job type, task run history, and taskflow runs by state through rda:// URIs), operator knowledge (runbooks, task type references, error and state code tables, an SLA guide, an operator toolkit, and request samples), and Agent Skills for failed job triage and job lifecycle control.

servers.name: IDMC Asset Documentation
servers.description: The IDMC Asset Documentation MCP server gives AI agents read-only access to Informatica Intelligent Data Management Cloud (IDMC) asset metadata, so that they can generate accurate, up-to-date technical documentation without manual API exploration.

toolDetails.name: idmc_agent_details_get
toolDetails.description: Returns the services and components of a Secure Agent by the agent ID.

toolDetails.name: idmc_agent_details_list
toolDetails.description: Returns details about every Secure Agent in the organization along with the services and components running on each. Use idmc_agent_details_get for a single agent.

toolDetails.name: idmc_agent_get_by_name
toolDetails.description: Returns the configuration details of a Secure Agent, including the agent ID, by name. Use the ID with idmc_agent_details_get.

toolDetails.name: idmc_agent_list
toolDetails.description: Returns a list of the names and IDs of every Secure Agent in the organization. Optionally, you can restrict to unassigned agents or include package and configuration details.

toolDetails.name: idmc_connection_get
toolDetails.description: Returns one connection's configuration by connection ID. Get IDs from idmc_connection_list. If you only have the connection name, use idmc_connection_get_by_name instead.

toolDetails.name: idmc_connection_get_by_name
toolDetails.description: Returns one connection's configuration by connection name. If you already have the connection ID, use idmc_connection_get instead.

toolDetails.name: idmc_connection_list
toolDetails.description: Returns every connection defined in the organization. You can use this tool to build a connection inventory. To get the configuration for a single connection, use idmc_connection_get or idmc_connection_get_by_name.

toolDetails.name: idmc_connection_metadata
toolDetails.description: Returns the runtime attributes of a connection for its source or target side, including each attribute's name, data type, default value, label, whether it is mandatory, maximum length, and possible values.

toolDetails.name: idmc_connection_search
toolDetails.description: Returns the connections associated with a Secure Agent or runtime environment, optionally filtered by connection UI type such as Oracle or Salesforce.

toolDetails.name: idmc_connection_source_objects
toolDetails.description: Returns the objects reachable through a connection, such as tables, files, or entities, from either the source or target side.

toolDetails.name: idmc_ingestion_file_activity
toolDetails.description: Returns File Ingestion and Replication job activity log entries. You can use the entries to document the run history of a file ingestion task. Requires taskId, runId, or both. To get the task ID, use idmc_ingestion_list_file_tasks or idmc_objects_search.

toolDetails.name: idmc_ingestion_get_file_task
toolDetails.description: Returns configuration details for one File Ingestion and Replication task by ID, including source and target connections, file transfer parameters, and the assigned runtime environment. To get the task ID, use idmc_objects_search (asset type MI_TASK) or an activity log entry. This tool doesn't resolve mapping tasks (MTT).

toolDetails.name: idmc_ingestion_list_file_tasks
toolDetails.description: Returns every File Ingestion and Replication task in the organization. Set resolveLocation to true to include each task's project and folder path.

toolDetails.name: idmc_mapping_get_by_name
toolDetails.description: Returns one mapping's configuration, including its v2 ID, by name. Use the ID with idmc_mapping_get_details.

toolDetails.name: idmc_mapping_get_details
toolDetails.description: Returns a mapping's configuration by v2 mapping ID, including source and target objects and properties, transformations, functions and expressions, parameters and default values, pre/post SQL, run-time conditions, and dependent tasks, the input for a natural language mapping description. Use the v2 ID only. IDs returned by idmc_objects_search are rejected with a 403 error.

toolDetails.name: idmc_mapping_get_transformation_details
toolDetails.description: Returns details for each transformation for a mapping by mapping ID, for use in the body of generated documentation. Optionally filter to a single transformation type.

toolDetails.name: idmc_mapping_get_transformation_details_by_name
toolDetails.description: Returns additional transformation detail for a mapping identified by name, optionally limited to one transformation type.

toolDetails.name: idmc_mapplet_get
toolDetails.description: Returns one PowerCenter mapplet's definition by mapplet ID. If you only have the mapplet name, use idmc_mapplet_get_by_name instead.

toolDetails.name: idmc_mapplet_get_by_name
toolDetails.description: Returns one PowerCenter mapplet's definition by mapplet name. If you already have the mapplet ID, use idmc_mapplet_get instead.

toolDetails.name: idmc_mapplet_list
toolDetails.description: Returns every PowerCenter mapplet in the organization for building a mapplet inventory.

toolDetails.name: idmc_mtt_get
toolDetails.description: Returns a mapping task's configuration snapshot by v2 task ID, including parameters, runtime overrides, and schema mode, for use in generated documentation. The response also carries mappingId (v2 id of the underlying mapping, for idmc_mapping_get_details) and frsGuid (global id, for idmc_objects_dependencies). Get task IDs from idmc_task_list_by_type with type MTT.

toolDetails.name: idmc_mtt_get_by_name
toolDetails.description: Returns one mapping task's configuration, including its ID, by name. Use the ID with idmc_mtt_get.

toolDetails.name: idmc_objects_dependencies
toolDetails.description: Returns the direct upstream (uses) or downstream (usedBy) references of an asset by global ID. Call repeatedly, using each returned asset's global ID as the next request's ID, to walk multiple layers of a dependency graph, the API itself returns only one hop per call. Takes global IDs only from idmc_objects_search, or frsGuid from idmc_mtt_get. Project IDs aren't accepted.

toolDetails.name: idmc_objects_lookup
toolDetails.description: Resolves assets from their project path and type to their global IDs. Use the IDs with tools that take an asset ID.

toolDetails.name: idmc_objects_search
toolDetails.description: Searches the IDMC asset catalog for projects, folders, mappings, tasks, connections, and other assets using a FIQL filter. Returns global IDs using 22 characters. These work with idmc_objects_dependencies but not with the v2 tools (idmc_mtt_get, idmc_mapping_get_details, idmc_taskflow_get_linear), which need the v2 ID from idmc_task_list_by_type or from a tool that finds assets by name.

toolDetails.name: idmc_runtime_get
toolDetails.description: Returns one runtime environment's configuration and assigned agents by ID. If you only have the environment name, use idmc_runtime_get_by_name instead.

toolDetails.name: idmc_runtime_get_by_name
toolDetails.description: Returns one runtime environment's configuration and assigned agents by name. If you already have the environment ID, use idmc_runtime_get instead.

toolDetails.name: idmc_runtime_list
toolDetails.description: Returns every runtime environment in the organization for building an environment inventory. To get configuration and assigned agents for a single environment, use idmc_runtime_get.

toolDetails.name: idmc_source_control_commit_history
toolDetails.description: Returns the source-control commit history of an asset, newest first, with commit hashes. Use the hashes with idmc_source_control_compare_versions.

toolDetails.name: idmc_source_control_compare_versions
toolDetails.description: Compares two versions of a source-controlled asset and returns line-level differences for generating change documentation between releases. Set source and destination to a commit hash, or to CURRENT-VERSION for a version that hasn't been checked in. Set outputFormat to JSON for structured differences or TEXT for Git diff text.

toolDetails.name: idmc_task_list_by_type
toolDetails.description: Returns the name and v2 ID of every task of the given type for building a task inventory or resolving a task name to the v2 ID that idmc_mtt_get needs. Dynamic mapping tasks (DTT) and taskflows aren't supported types. To find them, use idmc_objects_search.

toolDetails.name: idmc_taskflow_get_linear
toolDetails.description: Returns one linear taskflow's configuration by v2 taskflow ID (WORKFLOW assets only; not TASKFLOW or PROCESS assets). Get IDs from idmc_taskflow_list_linear. If you only have the taskflow name, use idmc_taskflow_get_linear_by_name instead.

toolDetails.name: idmc_taskflow_get_linear_by_name
toolDetails.description: Returns one linear taskflow's configuration by taskflow name (WORKFLOW assets only; not TASKFLOW or PROCESS assets). The response includes the v2 id. If you already have the taskflow ID, use idmc_taskflow_get_linear instead.

toolDetails.name: idmc_taskflow_list_linear
toolDetails.description: Returns every linear taskflow in the organization. Use the returned IDs with idmc_taskflow_get_linear.

toolDetails.name: idmc_taskflow_status_list
toolDetails.description: Returns run statuses of published taskflows for monitoring, optionally filtered by run ID, run status, or a start/end time window. Omit all parameters to list recent taskflow runs. To get a list of taskflows, use idmc_objects_search with type=='TASKFLOW'.

servers.description: Entire IDMC data management planner MCP server. When a user adds this planner MCP, IDMC orchestrates the full data-management flow — discovery, data exploration, data quality, and other data-management skills. The user does not need to think about orchestration.

servers.name: Ingestion and Replication Management
servers.description: Discovers ingestion task modes and properties, generates CDC scripts, validates and creates Database and Application Mass Ingestion tasks.

servers.name: Log Management
servers.description: Retrieves historical Data Integration activity logs, session logs, and error logs from the Informatica IDMC Monitor service.

toolDetails.name: get_error_log
toolDetails.description: Retrieves the error log for a specific activity log entry. An empty response body indicates that the job completed without any error records.

toolDetails.name: get_session_log
toolDetails.description: Retrieves the session log for a specific activity log entry. If you specify an item ID or child item ID, retrieves the session log for that item. For a single-task job, the response is in plain text. For a multi-task job, supplying the item ID and child item ID targets the session log for a specific subtask.

toolDetails.name: search_activity_log
toolDetails.description: Searches activity log entries for completed Data Integration jobs. All parameters are optional. You can filter by log entry ID or task. When used together, taskID and runID search for a specific completed job.

servers.name: Master Data Exploration Skill
servers.description: Single-tool MCP exposing the CLAIRE mdmSkill — query mastered entities and golden records across Customer, Product, and Provider domains.

servers.name: MDM Configuration Authoring
servers.description: Access to MDM SaaS entity configuration and master data: entity schemas, match rules, source systems, source ranking, enrichment providers, and master record details, history and data quality.

toolDetails.name: get_business_entity_doc
toolDetails.description: Returns the full definition document of a business entity by its identifier, for example c360.person. Content is translated (localized) and includes system fields tagged master. Returns 404 if no business entity exists for the id.

toolDetails.name: get_data_quality
toolDetails.description: Retrieves data quality rules and results for a master record identified by business id, using its business entity GUID and the current model version.

toolDetails.name: get_entity_folder
toolDetails.description: Returns the id and name of the project containing an FRS base entity (document or folder), or null if it has none.

toolDetails.name: get_entity_history_feed
toolDetails.description: Returns the history feed of a business entity record: its create, merge and unmerge events up to the given end time, with every event keyed by event id and arranged on a timeline of years and months. Returns up to 1000 events, excluding pending changes.

toolDetails.name: get_entity_schema_full
toolDetails.description: Returns the full schema definition of a business entity, including its fields and configuration, identified by the entity's internal id (for example c360.person).

toolDetails.name: get_entity_xref
toolDetails.description: Reads one cross-reference (xref) record of a business entity: the source record identified by its source system and its primary key in that source system, which contributes data to a business entity record. Returns the xref type, the business ID of the business entity record it belongs to, and the record's field values as a list of key/value entries.

toolDetails.name: get_match_pairs
toolDetails.description: Returns the match pairs generated for a master record's match group. Looks up the member source records (source system and source primary key) of the master record identified by business entity type and business id, then lists the match pairs involving those source records.

toolDetails.name: get_match_rules
toolDetails.description: Retrieves the match configuration for a business entity: its indexes, match rule sets, and the fields used for matching, including both published and draft match models.

toolDetails.name: get_provider_definition
toolDetails.description: Retrieves a single MDM provider definition by its GUID, returning the full provider record.

toolDetails.name: get_public_entity
toolDetails.description: Returns the active master record of a business entity, identified by its entity type and business id.

toolDetails.name: get_public_entity_members
toolDetails.description: Returns the member source records of the active master record of a business entity, identified by its entity type and business id. Each member has its source system and its primary key in that source system. The full list is returned in a single response.

toolDetails.name: get_related_entities
toolDetails.description: Returns records related to a given record, with relationship details. Returns up to 50 related records (first page).

toolDetails.name: get_source_ranking_templates
toolDetails.description: Lists the source ranking templates defined in the MDM configuration, one page at a time. Each template gives its identifier, label, and the ordered source systems (rank 0 is highest).

toolDetails.name: get_source_trail
toolDetails.description: List per-field trust entries (source system, trust score, method, last updated, manual override) for a business entity record, excluding the root and zero-trust fields.

toolDetails.name: list_enrichment_providers
toolDetails.description: Lists the MDM enrichment providers available to the current user.

toolDetails.name: list_entity_types
toolDetails.description: Lists business entity types (internalId and name), such as Person and Organization, one page at a time. Follow pagination.hasMore to fetch more.

toolDetails.name: list_projects
toolDetails.description: Lists the projects available to the current user. Returns the id and name of each project.

toolDetails.name: read_codelist_lockstate

Returns lockState and primaryLockState once the state is UNLOCKED (no draft), LOCKED_AND_IN_PUBLISHING or LOCKED_AND_IN_DISCARDING. Use after publishing or discarding a draft to wait for completion. The call re-checks about once per second and can block up to about 30 seconds. If the code list is in LOCKED (open draft) or LOCKED_AND_IN_APPROVAL, it never matches and the call fails with 404 after about 30 seconds; a 404 can also mean the code list does not exist.

toolDetails.name: read_source_systems
toolDetails.description: Lists the source systems configured in the MDM model, returning each one's guid, name and English label. Returns up to 1000 source systems.

toolDetails.name: search_mdm
toolDetails.description: Runs a free-text search against business entity records and returns the matching results. Provide the business entity to search within and the free-text search string. Use an asterisk (*) to match all records. Returns up to 5 records from the first page of results.
