toolDetails.description: Sends a "claim" action for a specific task GUID. On success, the task moves from READY to RESERVED and is assigned to the authenticated caller.

toolDetails.name: create_be_record
toolDetails.description: Create one new business entity record, such as a Person, from the field values in payload. Field names and required fields are defined by the entity type's schema (see get_entity_schema). Not idempotent: each call creates a new record. On success the result gives the new record id. The result can say approvalRequired is true, which means the record is not final until it is approved.

toolDetails.name: create_relationship
toolDetails.description: Create one relationship that links two existing business entity records, such as an Organization that employs a Person. relationshipType selects the relationship type, which fixes the from and to entity types and the direction. _from and _to each identify a record as {"businessEntity": "<id of that record's entity type>", "id": {"sourceSystem": "...", "sourcePKey": "..."}}. A bare businessId shortcut, or an _from/_to.id that is a plain string instead of an object, is rejected; some wrong shapes return a generic 500 instead of a clear validation error, and nothing is created. Both records must already exist. Not idempotent: each call creates a new relationship.

toolDetails.name: delete_be_record
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Delete one existing business entity record, such as a Person, identified by its business id. This is a soft delete: afterwards reads by id and by source key return 404, but the record id is kept. There is no restore tool; creating the record again with the same sourceSystem and sourcePKey reuses the same id, holding only the newly supplied payload, and the old content does not return. The id is the record's business id, as returned by search or match results, not a source key. The result can say approvalRequired is true, which means the delete is not final until it is approved.

toolDetails.name: delete_relationship
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Delete one existing relationship between two records, identified by its business id. This removes the link only; the two linked records are not affected. sourceSystem is required. sourcePKey is optional, and if supplied it must be the relationship's own key in that source system, otherwise the request is rejected.

toolDetails.name: discard_bulk_correction
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Discard draft edits: delete the drafts and leave each record as it currently is. This cannot be undone: the drafted values are lost and would have to be drafted again with draft_bulk_correction. Takes draft ids (the changeList value from get_draft_status or the draft tools). The call returns HTTP 200 even when nothing was discarded: persistedAsActive true means the drafts were discarded; false means they were not, and messages.errors has an entry per failed draft with its message. A discarded draft no longer exists, and get_draft_status returns its record with state ACTIVE.

toolDetails.name: draft_bulk_correction
toolDetails.description: Create or update a draft of one text, date or other scalar field change on each given record, identified by its business id (_meta.businessId, such as MDM00000000005, from search_business_entity or match_records). Not for lookup (picklist) fields, whose value in the record is an object with a Code and for which get_lookup_values lists the allowed values; use draft_bulk_lookup_correction for those. Every record in one call gets the same change: the same field set to the same value. Only draft records the user has clearly identified. If a name or other partial reference matches more than one record, list the matches and ask which to change before calling this tool; edit all of them only when the user explicitly asks for every match. For replace and add, set exactly one of valueText, valueNumber and valueBoolean, matching the field's type in get_entity_schema (for a field inside a group, the type under items.properties); for remove, set none. To set different values, group the business ids by value and call this tool once per value. This writes drafts only: it does not change the records and does not submit anything. At most 50 business ids per call. A business id that does not exist is silently left out, so compare the number of results with the number of business ids you sent. On success the result has one entry per drafted record: businessId; changeList, the draft id that publish_bulk_correction and discard_bulk_correction take (collect the changeList values of all calls and pass them together); validation, PASSED or FAILED; draft, the record with the change applied; and base2draft, each changed field with its operation. On failure the call returns HTTP 400 with errorCode DRAFT.500001 and the reasons in errorDetail.details[].message.

toolDetails.name: draft_bulk_lookup_correction
toolDetails.description: Create or update a draft of one lookup (picklist) field change on each given record, identified by its business id (_meta.businessId, such as MDM00000000005, from search_business_entity or match_records). Lookup fields are those whose value in the record is an object with a Code, for example companyType or gender, and for which get_lookup_values lists the allowed values. Use draft_bulk_correction for text, date and other scalar fields. Get the allowed Code values from get_lookup_values first. Every record in one call gets the same change: the same field set to the same Code. Only draft records the user has clearly identified. If a name or other partial reference matches more than one record, list the matches and ask which to change before calling this tool; edit all of them only when the user explicitly asks for every match. To set different values, group the business ids by value and call this tool once per value. This writes drafts only: it does not change the records and does not submit anything. At most 50 business ids per call. A business id that does not exist is silently left out, so compare the number of results with the number of business ids you sent. On success the result has one entry per drafted record: businessId; changeList, the draft id that publish_bulk_correction and discard_bulk_correction take (collect the changeList values of all calls and pass them together); validation, PASSED or FAILED; draft, the record with the change applied; and base2draft, each changed field with its operation. On failure the call returns HTTP 400 with errorCode DRAFT.500001 and the reasons in errorDetail.details[].message.

toolDetails.name: extract_document
toolDetails.description: Sends a PDF, base64-encoded in the JSON body, and returns extracted text, tables, form fields, and vision requests: regions where text extraction looks unreliable, for a vision-capable model to re-read.

toolDetails.name: extract_documents_status
toolDetails.description: Get the status and result of document extractions started with extract_documents_submit. Returns one entry per job id with its jobId and a status of running, succeeded, failed or not_found (no job has this id; check the id and do not poll it again). A running job has no result yet, so call this again later; keep polling until every job is succeeded, failed or not_found. A succeeded job includes result, with the same content as extract_document: documentId, extractionMethod, pageCount, text, pages, tables, formFields, visionRequests, warnings and identity. A failed job includes errorMessage and error with a code such as unparseable_pdf when the file is not a readable PDF. Read-only: it does not search or change any MDM record.

toolDetails.name: extract_documents_submit
toolDetails.description: Start the extraction of several PDF documents, each base64-encoded in the JSON body, in one call. It does not wait for the content: it returns, in the order the files were sent, one entry per file with its filename, a status of accepted or throttled, and a jobId for accepted files. A throttled file has no jobId and was not started, so send it again later. Pass the jobIds to extract_documents_status to get the extracted content. It does not search or change any MDM record. To extract a single document and wait for the result, use extract_document.

toolDetails.name: filter_relationships
toolDetails.description: Find existing relationships of one type, optionally limited by the record at either end, for example every Employs link for a given Organization. filter holds an optional _from and an optional _to; give both to find the links between two records. Each result includes the relationship id and its _from and _to records. Read-only. Paged: use pageOffset to read the next page.

toolDetails.name: get_business_entity_by_id
toolDetails.description: Return the full current record for one business entity, such as a Person, by its business id. The id is the record's business id from search or match results, not a source system key; use get_business_entity_by_source_key for a source system key. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: get_business_entity_by_source_key
toolDetails.description: Return the full current record for one business entity, such as a Person, by its source system and the record's primary key in that source system (for example a CRM customer number). Use get_business_entity_by_id for a business id instead. If no record matches, the result is empty, which is a valid answer. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: get_completed_ingress_dq_jobs
toolDetails.description: List the most recent ingress jobs that finished successfully (state SUCCESS), newest first, with their data-quality counts, so you can spot an ingress that completed but still had records rejected. get_failed_jobs does not return these because the job did not fail. All kinds of ingress job are included (file import, API, and so on): a job counts as ingress when its jobDefinition.id contains 'ingress'. Each entry has id, name, jobDefinition (the job type id, e.g. internal.c360.ingress.fileImportJob), startedAt and completedAt (epoch milliseconds), durationMs (completedAt minus startedAt), startedBy, recordsIngressed (input rows), validationErrorRows (rows that failed validation), loadFailedRecords (records that failed to load) and metrics (every job-level metric, for counts not listed above). A job has data-quality errors when validationErrorRows or loadFailedRecords is greater than 0. limit is how many recent SUCCESS jobs of any type are scanned, so fewer ingress jobs than limit may come back; a count of null means the job did not report that metric. These counts come from the job summary only. A job that shows 0 can still have validation-rule failures that appear only in its step details, so call get_job_errors with the id of one job to confirm or to see per-step counts. COMPLETED is not a valid state filter; SUCCESS is the only 'completed successfully' state and is fixed in this tool. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: get_draft_status
toolDetails.description: Load the draft of each given record, identified by its business id (_meta.businessId, such as MDM00000000005), or the current record when it has no draft. The result has one entry per record found: businessId; changeList, the draft id that publish_bulk_correction and discard_bulk_correction take, present only when the record has a draft; validation, PASSED or FAILED, where FAILED means the draft breaks validation rules and the failed rules are in draft._cm.vader.fail; draft, the record with the draft changes applied; and base2draft, which lists each changed field with its operation (N new, U updated, D deleted) and who changed it, where changedBy EVO means the system recalculated that field. state is DRAFT for a draft, ACTIVE for a record with no draft, and CONFLICTS when the draft could not be submitted; error gives the reason. A business id that does not exist is silently left out, so compare the number of results with the number of business ids you sent. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: get_entity_schema
toolDetails.description: Return the JSON Schema for one business entity type, such as Person, identified by its internalId. schema.properties lists the field names, types, required fields, picklists and nested field groups. A field with type picklist accepts only values from a fixed list. To read those values, call get_lookup_values with this type's guid and the field's path as lookupFieldPath. The path is the chain of property keys leading to the field, joined with dots. A top-level field is just its key, for example prefixName. Where a key's value is an array (type array), continue into its items.properties, but do not put items or properties in the path: country under PostalAddress is PostalAddress.country, not PostalAddress.items.properties.country. Returns the type definition, not records. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: get_failed_jobs
toolDetails.description: Returns a page of job instances filtered by state, along with aggregate counts grouped by state. No state filter is applied automatically — pass state=FAILED to see only failed job instances. Only a single state value is supported per call. Page number is fixed at 0; use recordsPerPage to control how many records come back.

toolDetails.name: get_job_errors
toolDetails.description: Returns a fixed set of fields (id, name, _meta) for the job instance with the given id, including its step details. Use this to check whether a specific job failed and inspect its error state via _meta.

toolDetails.name: get_job_health_summary
toolDetails.description: Retrieves aggregated summary dashboard data covering job status, statistics, and code-list/meters reports, filterable by timeframe and job type.

toolDetails.name: get_job_history
toolDetails.description: Return daily history for one job type over a time window, for baseline comparison, for example how many records were ingested per day over the last 7 days. Pass from and to (epoch milliseconds) to choose the window; when they are omitted the backend uses its own default window. Returns reports.history (one bucket per day, each with a time and its numeric counts) and reports.jobDetails (recent jobs with their jobId, jobName and statistics). Optionally narrow to specific jobs with jobId, a list of job ids. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: get_lookup_values
toolDetails.description: List every value a lookup field accepts, as Code and Name pairs. The list is not filtered: a field that depends on another field, such as PostalAddress.state, returns all its values for every parent value. A lookup field accepts only these Code values; a Name that is not a Code is rejected. Each entry in content has Code (the stored value, for example {"Code": "M"}) and Name (the label a person sees, for example Male). The two can differ. numberOfElements, first and last indicate whether there are more pages. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: get_open_tasks
toolDetails.description: List the open MDM human tasks the caller can act on: tasks in the READY, RESERVED, IN_PROGRESS or SUSPENDED state. Takes no arguments: call it with an empty object. Returns tasks, at most 50, each with guid (the task id that claim_task, approve_task and reject_task take), applicationEvent, assetLabel, assetType, priority, assignee, initiatedBy, createdAt, dueDate, escalated, status, rawId, potentialOwnerGroup and primarySearchBy. For a record review task, primarySearchBy is the changelist id. The list is not filtered or de-duplicated. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: get_relationship
toolDetails.description: Return one relationship between two records by its business id, including its _from and _to records. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: list_entity_types
toolDetails.description: Return one page of business entity types (internalId, name and description), such as Person and Organization. Paged: pagination.hasMore is true when more types remain, and the next page is read by increasing offset by the number of types returned. The list contains type definitions only, not records. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: list_relationship_types
toolDetails.description: Return one page of relationship types (internalId, name, description, and the from and to business entity internalIds), such as Employs from Organization to Person. Paged: pagination.hasMore is true when more types remain, and the next page is read by increasing offset by the number of types returned. The list contains type definitions only, not relationship records. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: list_source_systems
toolDetails.description: Return one page of source systems (internalId, name and description). The internalId, not the name, is the value used as sourceSystem in write calls; the server does no name-to-internalId resolution. Paged: pagination.hasMore is true when more source systems remain, and the next page is read by increasing offset by the number returned. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: match_records
toolDetails.description: Find existing records that probably match one candidate, and return a match score for each. The candidate's field values go in data.searchRecord, using entity field names without a prefix. The active match rule requires at least one blocking field (for example fullName); without one the backend fails with a 'blocking field is mandatory' error, and firstName plus lastName alone is not always enough. searchControls optionally tunes the match; omit it to use backend defaults. A high score indicates likelihood, not certainty. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: publish_bulk_correction
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Submit draft edits so their changes take effect on the records. This changes real records and cannot be undone by this tool. Takes the sourceSystem the drafts were created with and draft ids (the changeList value from get_draft_status or the draft tools) of drafts whose validation is PASSED. Drafts with validation errors, and drafts whose record changed after the draft was made, are not submitted. The call returns HTTP 200 even when nothing was submitted: persistedAsActive true means the changes are now on the records; false means they are not, and messages.errors has one entry per failed draft with its draftId, a category such as DRAFT_PUBLISH_FAILED, and a message. approvalRequired true means the edits were sent for approval and have not taken effect yet. A submitted draft no longer exists, and get_draft_status returns its record with state ACTIVE. The result lists the submitted records and cross-references under messages.records and messages.xrefs, with their business ids and changed paths.

toolDetails.name: reject_task
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Rejects and completes an IN_PROGRESS human task, blocking the pending change. Claim and start it first; irreversible. Only after explicit steward rejection.

toolDetails.name: restart_job
toolDetails.description: Resumes the suspended MDM job instance identified by jobInstanceId, restarting it from the point of suspension.

toolDetails.name: search_business_entity
toolDetails.description: Full-text search for existing business entity records, such as a Person named Jon Smith. search takes name or key words, and wildcards such as * are allowed. entityType (an entity type id) is required and restricts the search to one type; search * with entityType lists every record of that type. filters narrows the results by field values, for example every Person whose gender is male; send search * with entityType and filters to list all records that match. Returns the matching records and hits, the number of matching records; use pageSize and pageOffset to read further pages. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: start_task
toolDetails.description: Start a claimed (RESERVED) human task, moving it to IN_PROGRESS. Call after claim_task and before approve_task or reject_task, which fail with ae.ht.complete.invalid.state otherwise.

toolDetails.name: update_be_record
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Replace the fields of one existing business entity record, identified by its business id. This is a full replace, not a partial update: any field left out of payload may be cleared, so payload must carry the complete record. Field names must match the entity type's schema. The result can say approvalRequired is true, which means the change is not final until it is approved.

toolDetails.name: update_relationship
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Replace the fields of one existing relationship between two records, identified by its business id. This is a PUT and a full replace: any field left out may be cleared, so send the complete relationship: _from and _to, plus every relationship field it should keep, such as effectiveStartDate, not only the changed ones. The result can say approvalRequired is true, which means the change is not final until it is approved.

servers.name: MDM Metadata Discovery
servers.description: Retrieves business entity definitions and their JSON Schemas from the MDM SaaS metadata service so AI agents can map incoming data to MDM structures.

servers.name: MDM Search
servers.description: Searches MDM SaaS business entity records with full-text keyword queries so AI agents can find existing master data before creating or updating records.

servers.name: resources_job_management
servers.description: Job Management MCP server with full end-to-end resource coverage: FILE, ZIP, and API resources across every supported format, alongside the complete Job Management tool set for orchestrating, monitoring, and managing Data Integration tasks and taskflows.

servers.name: Taskflow Administration
servers.description: Provides the capability to schedule and administer taskflows. When you add this MCP server, AI agents can list, create, assign, update, enable, disable, unassign, and delete schedules.

toolDetails.name: assign_taskflow_to_schedule
toolDetails.description: Attaches a Taskflow to an existing schedule so it runs on that recurrence, by creating a scheduler job that runs as the caller. It needs an existing schedule: create one with create_schedule or find one with list_schedules. The same schedule can serve many Taskflows, and its status (enabled or disabled) governs whether the Taskflow fires. Not idempotent: calling it again with the same taskflowName fails because job names are unique per org. Returns the new job id and name.

toolDetails.name: create_schedule
toolDetails.description: Creates a schedule only; nothing runs until a Taskflow is assigned. To schedule a Taskflow, call this tool, then assign_taskflow_to_schedule with the returned schedule id. Call list_schedules first to reuse an existing schedule. Not idempotent: each call creates another schedule. Returns the created schedule (HTTP 201) with its id.

toolDetails.name: delete_schedule
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes one schedule permanently by id; it cannot be undone. Fails with HTTP 500 (SCHEDULER_12001, asset is used by another asset) while any Taskflow job is still attached, so first remove each with unassign_taskflow_from_schedule. Returns 204 with no body.

toolDetails.name: get_taskflow_internal_url
toolDetails.description: Returns the in-cluster base URL of the Taskflow service for the caller's deployment group, as needed to schedule a Taskflow. Use the result as the taskflowInternalUrl input of assign_taskflow_to_schedule. Read-only; returns only the base URL string, not the full service registry.

toolDetails.name: get_taskflow_schedules
toolDetails.description: Lists the scheduler jobs that attach a Taskflow to its schedules, so you can see when and how it runs. Give the Taskflow design GUID; each result row is one scheduler job with its schedule expanded (job name, executeAs, serviceUrl, plus the schedule with its status, intervalType and start). An empty list means the Taskflow has no schedule. The same schedule can appear under many jobs. Use the job name from a row with unassign_taskflow_from_schedule. Read-only.

toolDetails.name: list_schedules
toolDetails.description: Lists the schedules (reusable recurrence definitions) of the caller's org; the org comes from the session. To see which schedules one Taskflow uses, call get_taskflow_schedules instead. Page with top and skip; add count=true for the total. Returns a value list; status is enabled or disabled.

toolDetails.name: unassign_taskflow_from_schedule
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes one scheduler job by name, so the Taskflow stops running on that schedule. Only the job is removed; the schedule itself and any other jobs on it stay. A job name that contains an apostrophe cannot be addressed and cannot be removed this way. Succeeds with HTTP 204 and no body.

toolDetails.name: update_taskflow_schedule
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Updates a Scheduler Service schedule (shared by all Taskflows assigned to it): its name, start/end, recurrence or time zone, and its enabled or disabled state via status (enabled or disabled). Always send the schedule's current name (get it from list_schedules): the Scheduler rejects updates without it. Only the fields sent change, and changes apply to every Taskflow assigned to the schedule. A disabled schedule keeps its assignments but does not run. Returns 204 with no body.

servers.name: Taskflow Asset Management
servers.description: Provides the capability to manage the deployment lifecycle of taskflows without opening the user interface. When you add this MCP server, AI agents can publish and unpublish one or many taskflows, track job results, and update the deployment settings such as the run API name.

toolDetails.name: delete_paramset
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes a parameter set by name. Irreversible: confirm the exact name with the user first.

toolDetails.name: get_asset_path
toolDetails.description: Retrieves a Taskflow asset's Project and Folder from its GUID, so that you can build the asset path (Explore/{Project}/{Folder}/{name}.TASKFLOW.xml) for publish_assets or unpublish_assets. Get the GUID from list_taskflows or list_assets_in_location.

toolDetails.name: get_paramset
toolDetails.description: Returns the file content of one parameter set by name.

toolDetails.name: get_publish_status
toolDetails.description: Retrieves per-asset status of a publish job; poll after publish_assets until jobState is SUCCESS or FAILED, then report each asset's outcome.

toolDetails.name: get_unpublish_status
toolDetails.description: Retrieves per-asset status of an unpublish job; poll after unpublish_assets until jobState is SUCCESS or FAILED, then report each asset's outcome.

toolDetails.name: list_assets_in_location
toolDetails.description: Lists the assets (taskflows, process objects) in a Project, or in a Folder of a Project, so you can see what exists at a location before acting on it. Give the Project name in project, plus the Folder name in folder for assets inside a Folder; omit folder for assets directly in the Project (assets in its Folders are not included). Names are case-sensitive. Results are paged: limit defaults to 50 and offset to 0, and the result carries totalCount and hasMore, so keep requesting with offset increased by limit until hasMore is false. Each asset is returned with name, type, GUID and assetPath, in the form Explore/{Project}/{Folder}/{name}.{TYPE}.xml (no Folder segment for Project-level assets). Use the GUID or assetPath with publish_assets, unpublish_assets or update_taskflow_metadata. If the Project or Folder does not exist, the result has an error message and the names that are available instead of assets; an existing location with no assets returns an empty assets list.

toolDetails.name: list_paramsets
toolDetails.description: Lists parameter sets with name, directory, file name and audit fields, without content. Page must be 1 or higher.

toolDetails.name: list_taskflows
toolDetails.description: Lists Taskflow assets in the org, filterable by publication status; it returns no project or folder, so use get_asset_path with the GUID to build the asset path for publish and unpublish. Supported MimeType: only taskflow (stored internally as application/xml+taskflow); other asset kinds are not listed by this tool.

toolDetails.name: publish_assets
toolDetails.description: Starts a bulk publish job for Taskflow asset paths taken from get_asset_path; then poll get_publish_status with the returned jobId until the job is final.

toolDetails.name: unpublish_assets
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Starts a bulk unpublish job for Taskflow asset paths taken from get_asset_path; then poll get_unpublish_status with the returned jobId until the job is final.

toolDetails.name: update_taskflow_metadata
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Updates deployment settings (API name, parameter set, and access lists) of Taskflows identified by GUID (assetType=Taskflow). Keys are exact and case-sensitive; unknown keys are silently ignored, so confirm the change took effect. Allowed Users and Allowed Groups replace the whole list; omitted keys are left unchanged. Keys: API Name (non-empty, 80 characters or fewer; only while unpublished); Parameter Set (letters, digits, _ - . and spaces, up to 255 characters); Allowed Users, Allowed Groups (names). Description, Run On and Tracing Level cannot be set for taskflows.

toolDetails.name: upload_paramset
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Creates a parameter set from parameter file text, or replaces an existing one when force is true. Write values as $$name=value. Scope comes from section headings inside the content, not from parameterDir: start with #USE_SECTIONS, then use [Global], [Project].[Folder].[Taskflow], or [Project].[Folder].[Taskflow].[Subtaskflow step]. The narrowest matching section wins.

servers.name: Data Quality Assets
servers.description: The Data Quality Assets server lets AI agents manage data quality assets from natural language. Use it to create dictionaries of reference values, load and maintain their data, and build, update, search, and delete cleanse assets that standardize your data.

toolDetails.name: append_dictionary_rows
toolDetails.description: Adds up to 10,000 rows to a dictionary; call finish_dictionary_upload once after the last batch to make the data available. For more than 10,000 rows call repeatedly, then finish once. Appends are not idempotent: if a batch fails or its outcome is unknown, don't blindly retry (rows would duplicate) — call clear_dictionary_rows, re-append all batches, then finish. If search_assets (type=DICTIONARY) returns more than one dictionary with that name, ask the user which one (by Project/Folder) before calling.

toolDetails.name: clear_dictionary_rows
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes all data rows from a dictionary while keeping its definition. Data quality assets keep using the last published data until finish_dictionary_upload is called. Calling finish_dictionary_upload without appending new rows first publishes an empty dictionary, so confirm that's what the user wants. Confirm the dictionary ID/name with the user first (use search_assets with type=DICTIONARY to look it up). If search_assets (type=DICTIONARY) returns more than one dictionary with that name, ask the user which one (by Project/Folder) before calling.

toolDetails.name: create_cleanse
toolDetails.description: Creates a new cleanse in a project or folder and returns it, including its id. ALWAYS send type=CLEANSE (required). Before building the cleanse, read the MCP resource infa-skill://dq-cleanse-authoring.zip (resources/read) for the authoring workflow, and its cleanse-model-format.md for the exact definition format and the step catalog. The service validates the definition itself when you call this tool. Before calling, show the user the cleanse name, the save location (Project or Project/Folder) and its inputs, steps and outputs, and call only after the user explicitly approves. Ask again if any of these change. A 409 means a cleanse with that name already exists at that location: suggest a new name and ask before retrying. ALWAYS send docRefIds: the id of every dictionary the cleanse uses, each once (take each id from the search_assets result you used to build it), or an empty list when there are none. They must match the dictionaries in the definition. A missing id is not caught by validation but leaves the cleanse without its dependency. The definition is a typed object (see the schema). Ask the user only for the options a step actually needs and has not stated: collect them all in ONE message, and never ask for an option that does not apply to that step type (e.g. no case sensitivity for custom strings, no dictionary column for a plain custom-string step). Never default any option. This covers step type, case type, delimiters, uppercase policy, trim/multiple-spaces flags, operation mode, scope, case sensitivity (dictionary modes only), dictionary and validColumn, replacement text, and merge inputs, order, delimiter and merged output name. The merge delimiter (joinChar) must be one of: space, tab, @ , - " / . # | ; ' _ . If the user asks for a different one (for example $), do not send it and do not substitute another: tell them it is not supported and ask them to choose one from the list. toolDetails.name: create_dictionary
toolDetails.description: Creates an empty Cloud Data Quality dictionary from a name and a list of columns, optionally in a specific project or folder, and returns its ID. Not idempotent: if a create times out, look the dictionary up (search_assets with type=DICTIONARY) before retrying, since a retry with the same name fails with 409.

toolDetails.name: delete_cleanse
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Deletes one cleanse permanently; it can't be undone. Find the id with search_assets (type=CLEANSE) first. If more than one cleanse has the name, list each match's name and path (Project/Folder) and ask the user which one; never choose yourself. Before calling, tell the user the cleanse name and its Project/Folder and call only after the user explicitly confirms the deletion. Never delete several cleanses from one confirmation unless the user listed them all. A cleanse that other assets reference is not deleted: the call fails with 424 ERR_ASSET_IN_USE and a references list. Tell the user which assets use it and don't retry.

toolDetails.name: delete_dictionary
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Permanently deletes a dictionary with all its data rows and stored files; fails with 409 ERR_DICTIONARY_IN_USE and the list of referencing assets if any data quality asset still uses it. Confirm the dictionary ID/name with the user first (use search_assets with type=DICTIONARY to look it up). If search_assets (type=DICTIONARY) returns more than one dictionary with that name, ask the user which one (by Project/Folder) before calling.

toolDetails.name: finish_dictionary_upload
toolDetails.description: Finalizes a dictionary upload: encrypts and stores the dictionary's current rows — after append_dictionary_rows and/or clear_dictionary_rows — in cloud storage, making the data available to data quality assets. Publishes exactly what is currently stored, even if that is empty (for example after a clear or a failed replace). Not needed after replace_dictionary_rows. Safe to repeat. If search_assets (type=DICTIONARY) returns more than one dictionary with that name, ask the user which one (by Project/Folder) before calling.

toolDetails.name: get_asset
toolDetails.description: Returns one Data Quality asset: the single read tool for every supported asset type, today a cleanse or a dictionary. For a dictionary it also returns its edit mode (customAttributes MODE: API or UI) and column names; check MODE before append_dictionary_rows, replace_dictionary_rows, clear_dictionary_rows or finish_dictionary_upload, which fail on a UI-mode dictionary. Only CLEANSE and DICTIONARY ids are supported. Send includeDefinition=true to get the definition: it comes back as a JSON STRING in nativeData.documentBlob, so parse it into an object. A dictionary's columns are in the parsed blob at readRelationalDSO.relationalFields[].name (for example Column 1); use the exact column name as validColumn. A cleanse's model is the parsed blob (inputs, outputs, instances, ...); edit it and send it back whole as the definition object to update_cleanse. The response has no docRefIds field: derive them from the parsed definition (every dictionary.frsId in operations and every dictionaries[].frsId in convert-case steps). The location is in parentInfo (Project, and Folder if any), the type in documentType, and customAttributes holds the stored attributes (DIMENSION). Find the id with search_assets first. Use this before update_cleanse.

toolDetails.name: replace_dictionary_rows
toolDetails.description: ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE: This operation cannot be undone. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool. | Replaces all rows of a dictionary with up to 10,000 new rows and publishes them in one step; this tool cannot read files or file paths, so the rows must be passed inline in the call, read from the file first; no finish_dictionary_upload call needed. Also discards any rows appended but not yet finished. If the call fails, assume the rows may already have been cleared: retry replace_dictionary_rows with the full data, and don't call finish_dictionary_upload, which would publish an empty or partial dictionary. Limited to 10,000 rows; for larger data use clear_dictionary_rows, then append_dictionary_rows in fixed batches of 1,000 rows (see that tool for the call count), then finish_dictionary_upload. Confirm the dictionary ID/name with the user first (use search_assets with type=DICTIONARY to look it up). If search_assets (type=DICTIONARY) returns more than one dictionary with that name, ask the user which one (by Project/Folder) before calling.

toolDetails.name: search_assets
toolDetails.description: Searches the Data Quality assets the user can access. This is the single search tool for every supported asset type; today CLEANSE and DICTIONARY. Results never include definitions. type is required: a single value, CLEANSE or DICTIONARY (one call per type). Use name for an exact match or nameStartsWith for a prefix match. Returns {value:[...]}; each item has id (the FRS id: pass it as assetId to get_asset, as cleanseId to update_cleanse and delete_cleanse, as dictionaryId to the dictionary tools, and as a docRefIds entry for dictionaries), name, documentType, documentState (VALID or INVALID), customAttributes, and parentInfo (the Project, and the Folder if any, e.g. [{parentType:Space,...},{parentType:Project,parentName:Default}]). Use it to find a cleanse by name before get_asset, update_cleanse or delete_cleanse, to find a dictionary by name before get_asset, set_dictionary_edit_mode, append_dictionary_rows, replace_dictionary_rows, clear_dictionary_rows, finish_dictionary_upload or delete_dictionary, to check that a cleanse name is free at a location (compare the parentInfo project/folder), and to find the id of every dictionary the cleanse uses. Several assets can share a name in different projects: list each by project and ask. Search results never include a cleanse's definition or a dictionary's columns: read them with get_asset (includeDefinition=true). Results are paged: at most limit assets (default 25, max 100) are returned per call. Prefer a narrow name or nameStartsWith filter and a small page (25 to 50) over loading everything; when a call returns limit assets there may be more, so fetch the next page with offset = previous offset + limit only if you need it. If nothing matches, value is empty; do not guess an id.

toolDetails.name: set_dictionary_edit_mode
